sources.title: Gary W. Oehlert, A First Course in Design and Analysis of Experiments
sources.locator: Chapter 13 §§13.1–13.3.2, printed pp.315–329 (PDF labels approximately pp.335–357). Focused reading: RCBD randomization/model and interaction degrees of freedom in §§13.2–13.2.2; Latin-square definition and restricted randomization in §§13.3–13.3.2.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete relevant author-hosted PDF passages. The text states that every treatment occurs once in each complete block and treatment assignments are independently randomized within blocks; gives the additive RCBD model; explains that with one observation per treatment-block cell the interaction/error term has no separately estimable pure-error degrees of freedom; defines Latin squares and describes restricted randomization. The exact F law is proved locally from the repository's published nested Gaussian linear-model theorem, not inferred from the source's ANOVA table.

contents.name: Complete-block treatment balance and independent within-block randomization
contents.support: Supports the complete-block structure and the independent treatment permutation law; the local definition states the exact finite probability mass function.

contents.name: Additive RCBD mean model and treatment analysis
contents.support: Supports the additive model and treatment F-statistic structure. Exact Gaussian distributional calibration is supplied by the cited proved local nested-model theorem.

contents.name: One response per treatment-by-block cell leaves interaction/error without separate pure-error degrees of freedom
contents.support: The source warns that unrestricted interaction consumes the residual degrees of freedom; the local proposition supplies the exact subspace and nonunique-decomposition proof.

contents.name: Latin-square row/column balance and restricted randomization
contents.support: Supports one treatment per row and column and the requirement to state the restricted randomization law. The authored definition explicitly chooses a uniform law on all Latin squares and proves its sample space is nonempty.

sources.title: Susan Holmes and Wolfgang Huber, Modern Statistics for Modern Biology
sources.locator: Chapter 13 §13.4.4, author-hosted full HTML chapter, lines 293–434; paired treatment as a special case of blocking, within-pair randomization, and paired-versus-unpaired comparison.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the full-text Chapter 13 passage covering blocking and pairing and its paired-versus-unpaired examples. The authors emphasize that pairing is a special case of blocking and that allocation within a pair should be randomized; their simulation is treated as illustration only, not as a proof of the finite-pair expectation or variance formulas.

contents.name: Paired experiment as a two-unit block and randomization within the pair
contents.support: Independent treatment of pairing and within-pair randomization; the exact design moments are derived by enumerating the two assignments locally.

contents.name: Paired-versus-unpaired simulations and dependence on block heterogeneity
contents.reason: The source's simulation motivates pairing but does not prove the fixed-potential-outcome randomization variance; the example calculation is verified from the local theorem.

sources.reading_verification: Inspected the full official NIST section. It supports general randomized-block context only. It does not discuss Latin-square allocations and is not used for any Latin-square claim or proof.

contents.name: Blocking on controlled nuisance factors and randomizing within blocks
contents.reason: Independent corroboration of the general block/randomize structure; the source is not used as a proof of the exact uniform permutation law.
